subject: MSA + Exhibit: finalize inspection scope, pen-test access windows, and evidence cadence
messages:
From: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@clearsky.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@clearsky.com>, Clearsky Health Legal <legal@clearsky.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Apr 2028 10:22:00 -0400
Subject: MSA redlines — security exhibit / pen test language and evidence cadence

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA. Attached are clearsky's initial redlines focused on the security exhibit and inspection language (attached as Clearsky_MSA_Redlines_20280416.pdf). High level asks from our side:

- Narrow the "inspection rights" carve to exclude operational PII and require sampled evidence sets rather than full tenant snapshots.
- Add a mutually-agreed SOC 2 sampling cadence (quarterly attestation windows + annual full-report delivery).
- Define pen-test access: ephemeral credentials, 48-hour notice, pre-agreed test window, and two-week remediation SLA for high severity.
- Clarify log-retention minimums and what we can expect in playbook handovers (audit logs, ephemeral KV cache access description).

We want to avoid a broad "unfettered access" clause — clearsky operates in a regulated environment and needs concrete guardrails. Laura, our counsel, will also review the technical appendix (SOC2-Appendix-v1.docx).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can do ephemeral staging access and a sampled evidence cadence? Also please flag any commercial implications for Reserved Capacity customers if we bake in timeboxed windows.

Thanks,
Emma

--
Emma Lewis
VP Legal, Clearsky Health
emma.lewis@clearsky.com
+1 415 555 0123

Attachments: Clearsky_MSA_Redlines_20280416.pdf (application/pdf), SOC2-Appendix-v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@clearsky.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Apr 2028 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — security exhibit / pen test language and evidence cadence

Emma — thanks for the detailed redlines and the appendix. Quick take from Redwood operations and legal grounds:

1) Ephemeral staging access — yes, supported. We provide timeboxed, audited credentials scoped to a staging environment and granular S3/DB view-only roles. We'll propose a standard ephemeral-access checklist (see attached PenTest-Access-Checklist.xlsx) to bake into the exhibit.

2) Sampled evidence cadence — we can commit to a sampling model for tenant-level artifacts; recommend quarterly sampling with an annual comprehensive SOC 2 package. Need legal to confirm minimum SLA on evidence delivery (we typically do 10 business days for standard requests).

3) Pen-test SLA/remediation — Ops can commit to triage within 48 hours and target remediation timelines, but remediation SLA for customer/third-party code will be exception-based. We'll map out what constitutes "high severity" in the exhibit.

Laura — please review the proposed language below and the attached checklist, then advise on any redline we should accept/ counter. Marissa — can you confirm whether Reserved Capacity support or DGA (dedicated GPU allocation) commitments change when we schedule pen-test windows? If so, call that out.

Proposed next steps: legal sync tomorrow (30m), then a joint technical call with Clearsky to walk the pen-test access runbook. If we align, we can push a clean MSA+exhibit to DocuSign by end of week.

Best,
Karthik
Director, GTM & Strategic Contracts
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1 650 555 0199

Date: Tue, 17 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: MSA redlines — security exhibit / pen test language and evidence cadence

Karthik — looping in Ops and Security for operational confirmations. Quick operational notes:

- We already support ephemeral staging credentials via our staging accounts and rotate creds automatically; we can add a 7-day window option on request.
- For sampling, suggest: quarterly sampled evidence (up to 3 sample artifacts per quarter) + annual complete SOC 2 bundle. Samples delivered within 10 business days after request.
- Pen-test execution: we require a pre-approved test plan and an isolated staging environment. No production access permitted unless explicitly agreed and scheduled under a separate SLA.
- Reserved Capacity customers: if a pen-test requires dedicated GPU cycles, we'll treat that as a billable time-block outside the committed baseline (we should surface any costs to the customer).

Legal: redlines I'd accept in principle — I'd suggest tightening the language around data minimization during evidence requests and adding a clause preventing offsite retention beyond agreed retention windows.

I'll be available for the sync tomorrow at 11:00 PT.

-Marissa
Senior Manager, Security Operations
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: MSA redlines — security exhibit / pen test language and evidence cadence

Thanks Marissa — that aligns with our expectations. A couple clarifications from our side before the sync:

- The sampling approach is acceptable so long as it's clearly defined in the exhibit (we'll mark sample artifact types in our redline).
- Two-week remediation SLA for "high" findings is a hard requirement for our InfoSec team — if Redwood can meet a two-week remediation target for platform issues, clearsky will accept exceptions for customer-owned code.
- On costs: clearsky is OK with discrete billable blocks for dedicated test cycles; we just want transparency up front.

I'll update the attached redline to reflect the sampling language and send a clean file before the meeting. Can we confirm the meeting for 11:00 PT tomorrow?

Best,
Emma

Date: Fri, 19 Apr 2028 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — security exhibit / pen test language and evidence cadence

Emma / team — following our internal review, Redwood is prepared to accept the proposed sampling cadence (quarterly samples + annual SOC2 package) with the following redline language to be inserted in the exhibit: 

- "Evidence requests shall be limited to sampled artifacts as defined in Appendix A. Redwood will deliver selected artifacts within 10 business days of a validated request. Requests for full-tenant artifacts require separate written agreement and may be subject to additional charges and data minimization conditions."

- "Penetration testing may be conducted in a mutually agreed staging environment under ephemeral credentials. High severity findings will be triaged within 48 hours and, to the extent caused by Redwood platform defects, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to remediate within fourteen (14) calendar days. Remediation for third-party or customer-controlled code remains outside Redwood's remediation obligations and will be handled per separate change control procedures."

- We will add an express prohibition on offsite retention of sampled PII beyond agreed retention windows and require that any extracted logs be redacted prior to transfer unless a specific exception is granted in writing.

If that language looks acceptable to Clearsky, please confirm and we will prepare a clean MSA+exhibit for signature (DocuSign link to follow). Karthik / Marissa: on the billing note, Ben — please pick the standard charge codes for dedicated-test windows and we will share with Clearsky in the meeting.

Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference
